locations.name: Bradbury Mountain State Park
locations.description: Rolling summit-loop trails and a mountain-bike pump track make Bradbury a reliable go-to for a first overnight or a quick afternoon hike. The open summit ledges are a favorite spot for a pack's first taste of real elevation.
locations.amenities: Cell Phone Service, Pit Latrines, Pavilion or Shelter

locations.name: Sebago Lake State Park Group Camp
locations.description: A full-service group campground on the lake's sandy south shore, with a swim beach and boat launch a short walk from every site — the district's default choice for a weekend campout that needs real plumbing.
locations.programs: Cub Scouts, Scouts BSA, Venturing, Sea Scouting
locations.amenities: Flush Toilets, Showers, Running Water, Electricity, Pavilion or Shelter

locations.name: Wolfe's Neck Center
locations.description: Working farm and forest trails along the Harraseeket River, with rustic cabins available for a low-key overnighter. Popular for Webelos den campouts that want structure without a full tent setup.
locations.amenities: Cabins, Running Water, Pit Latrines, Pavilion or Shelter

locations.name: Sebago Lake Land Reserve
locations.description: The Sebago Lake Land Reserve is a 1700-acre Land Reserve, located in Standish, that is open to the public for passive recreational activities. Most portions of the Land Reserve contain trails, including the Sebago to the Sea Trail and the Mountain Division Trail. The most contiguous trail network is housed within the Otter Ponds parcel. Trail maps are also available at any of the twelve kiosks, or you can pick one up at the Sebago Lake Ecology Center.
locations.types: Hiking, Boating, Swimming, Fishing, Camping, Overnighter/Lock-in
locations.amenities: Cabins, Flush Toilets, Showers, Electricity, Cell Phone Service, Running Water, Pavilion or Shelter, Tent Platforms

locations.name: Scarborough Marsh Nature Center
locations.description: Guided canoe trips through Maine's largest salt marsh, with tidal creeks calm enough for a den's first time in a boat. A short, scenic outing that pairs well with a nature-study requirement.
locations.amenities: Pit Latrines, Cell Phone Service

locations.name: Pineland Farms
locations.description: Groomed trail network across open farmland, used for cross-country skiing and snowshoeing in winter and hiking or biking the rest of the year. Equipment rentals available on site.
locations.types: Hiking, Biking, Snowshoeing, Skiing, Day Trip
locations.amenities: Flush Toilets, Running Water, Pavilion or Shelter, Cell Phone Service

locations.name: Crystal Lake Camp
locations.description: A small, quiet lakefront property well suited to a Cub Scout pack's first overnight — shallow swim area, easy cabin sleeping, and a short drive from most of the district.
locations.amenities: Cabins, Flush Toilets, Showers, Electricity, Running Water

locations.name: Baxter Woods Preserve
locations.description: A 30-acre urban forest preserve with an easy interpretive loop — ideal for a weeknight den meeting that wants to get outside without leaving the peninsula.
locations.amenities: Cell Phone Service

locations.name: Woods Road Community Forest
locations.description: 5.25 mile trail system; trails are often rooty and rocky and contain sections of narrow bridging over wet areas; Ladyslipper Trail at Woods Road entrance is a 1/4 mile accessible loop trail that is wider with a flat crushed stone and stone dust surface.
locations.amenities: Flush Toilets, Cell Phone Service, Running Water, Pavilion or Shelter

locations.name: Sebago Lake YMCA Cove
locations.description: A YMCA camp property available to Scouting groups by reservation, with a protected cove for small-boat sailing and canoeing and a full set of waterfront amenities.
locations.programs: Cub Scouts, Scouts BSA, Venturing, Sea Scouting
locations.amenities: Cabins, Flush Toilets, Showers, Electricity, Running Water, Tent Platforms, Pavilion or Shelter, Cell Phone Service

locations.name: Long Pond Camping Loop
locations.description: A no-frills backcountry-style loop for troops working toward a genuine wilderness campout — no cell coverage, no running water, just tent platforms and a quiet pond for fishing.
locations.amenities: Pit Latrines, Tent Platforms
